title: Disney Sues the Government, Saying It's Being Punished for Its News
summary:
What if you said something a powerful person didn't like, and then they tried to take away your stuff? That's what Disney says is happening to them.

Disney owns ABC, a big TV network. ABC has eight local TV stations across the US. Normally, the government gives licenses for these stations to operate. But now, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) wants to review those licenses early. Disney says that's not normal—it's because President Trump is angry at ABC's news coverage.

The lawsuit, filed in Washington, DC, says the Trump administration has attacked ABC's reporting many times. The president even posted on social media that ABC "should lose their Licences for their unfair coverage." The FCC says the early review is because of Disney's diversity programs and an investigation into the talk show "The View." But Disney thinks that's just an excuse.

Earlier this year, the FCC chairman said stations airing "fake news" could lose their licenses. Trump also demanded ABC fire late-night host Jimmy Kimmel for jokes he made about the first lady. Disney says this is all about punishing free speech.

Free speech groups are cheering Disney on. Seth Stern from the Freedom of the Press Foundation said it's about time someone took the FCC to court. He called the FCC chairman a "censorship tsar" who targets Trump's enemies. Disney wants a speedy hearing and a temporary order to stop the FCC. The news made Disney's stock go up. Now it's up to a judge to decide.
why_it_matters: This case is about whether big companies can be punished for news you watch at home, so it could affect how freely newsrooms report on powerful people.

The FCC (a government agency) gives TV and radio stations the licenses they need to broadcast on public airwaves.
The First Amendment of the U.S. Constitution protects free speech, which is why Disney says this case matters.
